summary.headline: Grasim Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR48,716 crore, up 21% YoY, with standalone EBITDA more than doubling to INR1,094 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue reached a record INR48,716 crore (up 21% YoY), the 24th consecutive quarter of YoY growth. Standalone revenue rose 28% to INR11,795 crore and standalone EBITDA rose 107% to INR1,094 crore. Birla Opus revenue grew 64% YoY to INR1,661 crore after an 8.8% cumulative price increase to offset a raw material cost shock, and Birla Pivot grew 75% to INR2,548 crore. Management also disclosed a new 0.25% of standalone revenue brand royalty payable to Birla Holdings from June 2026, and a planned Renewables equity infusion below INR1,000 crore in FY27.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated net debt to TTM EBITDA

segments.name: Birla Opus (paints)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,661 crore (+64% YoY, +17% QoQ); market share up 30 bps QoQ to a number-three position, with 8.8% cumulative price increase in Q1. Premium and luxury portfolio is about 65% of sales value; institutional sales up 85% YoY.

segments.name: Birla Pivot (B2B e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,548 crore (+75% YoY), annualised run rate above INR10,000 crore. Management reiterated EBITDA break-even by exit of FY27; private labels more than doubled YoY off a low base.

segments.name: Cellulosic fibres (VSF/CSF)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR4,530 crore (+12% YoY) on volumes down 4% YoY; specialty fibre rose to 27% of sales mix from 21%. EBITDA roughly doubled, helped by a low base and specialty mix.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,640 crore (+10% YoY); ECU realisation INR37,955/t (+6% YoY); caustic share of revenue fell to 49% and specialty chemicals rose to 30%. EBITDA INR491 crore (+16%). Volumes softer on plant maintenance.

segments.name: Cement (UltraTech, consolidated)
segments.commentary: Sales volume 41.31 Mt (+12% YoY); gray capacity 205.5 Mt after adding 8.7 Mt in the quarter; EBITDA INR5,146 crore (+12%). Green power mix 45.6%; 5,802 retail outlets.

segments.name: Aditya Birla Capital (financial services)
segments.commentary: Lending portfolio grew 32% to nearly INR2,20,000 crore; housing finance crossed INR50,000 crore (+50%). Grasim invested INR2,880 crore at INR356/share to maintain its fully diluted stake.

segments.name: Other businesses
segments.commentary: Renewables revenue +59% YoY; textiles +26% YoY; insulators serving the power sector expansion.

guidance_outlook: Birla Opus: continues to target INR10,000 crore revenue by FY28 and guides over 50% YoY revenue growth for FY27; expects to become profitable once it reaches INR10,000 crore.
Birla Pivot: on track for EBITDA break-even by exit of FY27 (earlier guidance tied break-even to about USD1 billion or INR8,500 crore revenue; timeline shifted slightly).
Standalone FY27 capex planned at INR3,157 crore (about 45% growth); Q1 spend INR375 crore (about 12% of budget).
Net debt to EBITDA to be kept below 2x for the entire year; Renewables equity contribution below INR1,000 crore in FY27; transaction expected to complete around December 2026.
Chlorine integration expected to reach 68% by exit of FY27 as CPVC is commissioned and ECH commissioning happens in Q2 FY27.
Opus Q2 FY27 expected to be weaker on monsoon seasonality and reversal of Q1 dealer stocking; management expects market stock to normalise by Q3.
capex_capacity: Lyocell Phase 1: INR1,350 crore, 55,000 TPA, detailed engineering and civil work progressing.
Lyocell Phase 2: INR3,094 crore, 110,000 TPA, approved and moving through environmental clearance.
Birla Opus manufacturing capacity 1,332 million litres per annum across six plants; Q1 was the highest-ever production with utilisation improving.
UltraTech: gray cement capacity 205.5 Mt including overseas after 8.7 Mt added in the quarter; renewable power capacity 1.4 GW.
demand_pricing: Birla Opus: raw material COGS up 20-25%, or 10-14% of revenue depending on month; price increases were phased, cumulative 8.8% in Q1 with part flowing into Q2. Management said Q1 was boosted by dealer channel stocking ahead of industry price hikes.
Birla Opus distribution: 12,100+ towns, 55,000+ dealers billed, 1,450+ exclusive franchise outlets, 228 products and 1,945 SKUs, about 11,000 institutional project sites billed in the quarter.
Birla Pivot: volumes supported by demand timing as customers bought at measured rates during Middle East volatility; repeat purchases and new buyer additions reported as rising.
CSF: China supply described as disciplined; management said Indonesian and other high-cost capacity closures are positive for global supply-demand balance.
Caustic: SE Asia caustic soda exited the quarter at USD483/t vs USD468/t a year earlier; management expects domestic prices to trade at import parity.

qa_highlights.question: Is Birla Opus's sequential growth of 17% in line with listed peers, and how should profitability and revenue be prioritised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 industry revenue was inflated by channel stocking ahead of double-digit price hikes; as a new entrant, Birla Opus lacks that stocking power. It will keep the INR10,000 crore revenue target and judge revenue over the longer term.

qa_highlights.question: Will Birla Opus turn profitable on a full-year FY28 basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the stand is unchanged: profitability begins once Birla Opus reaches INR10,000 crore revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 64% YoY growth give confidence on FY27 growth above 50%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to over 50% YoY revenue growth for FY27; annual dealer loyalty and year-end schemes are expected to add sales in later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 0.25% royalty to Birla Holdings and its impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Applicable from 1 June 2026 on standalone revenue, capped at INR225 crore. Management estimated about INR100 crore impact for standalone; on INR50,000 crore revenue it would be about INR125 crore. Subsidiaries pay on their own revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How will Grasim fund the Renewables equity contribution and what is the net debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Grasim's contribution in FY27 is under INR1,000 crore, with a cash impact of less than INR1,000 crore; GIP is also investing. Net debt to EBITDA will stay below 2x through the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for chemicals margins and caustic pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 margins will face pressure from higher-cost inventory bought in Q1, and it is pricing near daily against commodity prices. It sees domestic caustic trading at import parity and new PVC-linked capacity as small.

qa_highlights.question: Are VSF margins sustainable, and what is the impact of Lenzing exits?
qa_highlights.answer: VSF operating rates in India are close to 100% excluding maintenance. Management said competitor exits are small, high-cost capacity and that Indonesian capacity cuts help global supply-demand balance.

qa_highlights.question: When will Birla Pivot break even, and what share of sales comes from UBS stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Pivot is set to exit FY27 at EBITDA break-even, slightly later than earlier guidance. Retail is 15-20% of mix, and UBS is 70-75% of retail revenue.

risks_watch: Paints margins and share: price differential vs industry has narrowed; Q2 volumes may be weak due to monsoon and dealer destocking.
Commodity volatility: sulphur, caustic and cotton input costs, Middle East and Gulf conflict affecting shipping and feedstock; chemicals faces Q2 margin pressure from expensive Q1 inventory.
Caustic soda price correction risk from new Indian capacity, despite management's view that import parity will hold.
Renewables (AB Renewables) capital needs and debt levels; a separate analyst session has been promised with the company team.
Birla Pivot EBITDA break-even timing, which has already slipped slightly versus earlier guidance.
Royalty payable to Birla Holdings starting June 2026 adds a cost line for standalone.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and market share, with management stressing that the business is being built for the long term. Cautious and openly hedged on Q2 paints volumes, chemicals margins and commodity direction, and deferred the detailed AB Renewables questions to a separate session.
key_quotes: In quarter one FY27, we achieved highest ever revenues of INR48,716 crores with a year-over-year growth of 21%.
We will prioritize market share gains and we will deliver the revenues we have guided to.
Birla Pivot remains on track to achieve EBITDA break-even by exit of FY27.
We will be maintaining our net debt below two.

adds.what: UltraTech gray cement capacity addition of 8.7 Mt in Q1 (now 205.5 Mt incl. overseas)

growth.why: Management guides Birla Opus FY27 revenue growth above 50% and a INR10,000 crore Opus brand by FY28, plus Pivot EBITDA break-even by FY27 exit; backing is partial, with Opus growth tied to price increases and dealer stocking, Lyocell capacity still years from output, and UltraTech's 8.7 Mt addition already live.
